title: Vascular insult to the brain
summary: Vascular insult to the brain (stroke), characterized by A) sensory/motor aphasia, B) motor function disorganization in two extremities, or C) marked limitation in physical functioning AND in one of four mental functioning areas — in each case persisting for at least 3 consecutive months after the insult.

children.criterion: Documented vascular insult to the brain (stroke, ICH, SAH, etc.)
Paragraph A (aphasia), B (motor function), or C (marked limitation + mental area)
Sensory or motor aphasia resulting in ineffective speech or communication (see 11.00E1), persisting for at least 3 consecutive months after the insult

Disorganization of motor function in two extremities (see 11.00D1), resulting in an extreme limitation (see 11.00D2) in the ability to stand up from a seated position, balance while standing or walking, or use the upper extremities, persisting for at least 3 consecutive months after the insult
Marked limitation (see 11.00G2) in physical functioning (see 11.00G3a) AND in one of four mental functioning areas, both persisting for at least 3 consecutive months after the insult
Marked limitation in ONE of four mental functioning areas
Marked limitation in understanding, remembering, or applying information (see 11.00G3b(i))
Marked limitation in interacting with others (see 11.00G3b(ii))
Marked limitation in concentrating, persisting, or maintaining pace (see 11.00G3b(iii))
Marked limitation in adapting or managing oneself (see 11.00G3b(iv))
Both the physical limitation and the mental limitation persisting for at least 3 consecutive months after the insult
